africa-post-colonial-1.l1: Draw a one-page timeline of 1880 to 1914 with at least eight dated events from the lesson. Mark which events the historians treat as the start of the Scramble, and write how the choice changes the story you tell.
africa-post-colonial-1.l2: Choose one treaty from the lesson. List who signed it, who could read it and what each side later said it meant. Then rate the treaty as evidence using the evidence tags.
africa-post-colonial-1.l4: Write a two-paragraph source note on the Congo Free State death toll. Give the range, who produced each estimate and why the figures differ, then say which figure you would quote and with what warning.

africa-post-colonial-2.l1: Reread the worked example on the official history. Write three things an official history of Maji Maji would leave out, and name two other kinds of source a historian would want to set beside it.
africa-post-colonial-2.l2: Make a two-column table of the figures given for the Herero and Nama war. For each figure write who counted, when, and what the count includes or leaves out.
africa-post-colonial-2.l3: Choose one group in the Mau Mau conflict: fighters, loyalists or civilians. Write what a colonial government archive would tell you about them, what it would not, and where else you would look.

africa-post-colonial-3.l1: Using the dates in the lesson, work out the years between each Pan-African Congress named there. Write what pattern the gaps show and what could explain it.
africa-post-colonial-3.l3: Choose Negritude, the Manchester Congress of 1945 or Accra in 1958. Write a 100-word account of what it changed, then name the evidence that shows the change and rate that evidence.
africa-post-colonial-3.l4: List the principles the lesson names in the OAU Charter. For each one, write one question a historian would ask to test whether it was followed in practice.

africa-post-colonial-4.l2: Write a short comparison of the British and French routes to independence in the lesson. Say who set the timetable in each case and what that meant for the new state.
africa-post-colonial-4.l3: Work out the length of the Algerian war from the start and end dates in the lesson, showing the arithmetic. Write one sentence saying which dates you chose and why.
africa-post-colonial-4.l4: Read the two independence-day speeches as the lesson teaches, for aims and not results. List the aims each speaker states, then write which speech is easier to judge and why.
africa-post-colonial-4.l5: Choose one leader named in the lesson. Judge the leader as a success or failure under each of the two definitions of failure in the worked example, and write which verdict you trust more.

africa-post-colonial-5.l1: Make a table of the laws and land measures the lesson names from before 1948. For each, give the date, what it did and who it affected most.
africa-post-colonial-5.l2: Choose three of the apartheid laws in the lesson. For each, write what it controlled in daily life, who it affected and what contradiction inside the system it shows.
africa-post-colonial-5.l3: Run the check from the worked example on a second official figure from the lesson. Write what the figure counts, who published it and what it would not show.
africa-post-colonial-5.l4: Write a timeline from 1976 to 1994 with at least ten dated entries from the lesson, and check every date against the text. Mark the entries a negotiator would have counted as turning points.

africa-post-colonial-6.l1: Write down the range of death-toll figures given for the Biafran war. For each, give who produced it and why it differs, then say which you would quote and with what warning.
africa-post-colonial-6.l2: Repeat the width-of-range exercise on a second figure from the lesson on the Derg and the famine. Show the arithmetic and write what the width tells you about the evidence.
africa-post-colonial-6.l3: Summarise the three diagnoses of the economic crisis in a table: who wrote each, what it blamed and what it recommended. Write one point where all three readings meet.
africa-post-colonial-6.l4: Choose one claim about what held African economies back. Run the causal-claim test from the worked example on it, and write what other factors a careful historian would need to rule out.

africa-post-colonial-7.l2: Work out the toll of the 1994 genocide under two different baselines, as in the worked example. Write which baseline the sources support and what each choice changes.
africa-post-colonial-7.l3: Pick one court or institution named in the lesson. Write what it was set up to do and one criticism a critic would make of how it worked, then say what evidence would test that criticism.
africa-post-colonial-7.l5: Find a recent news claim about Sudan, South Sudan or the Sahel. Run the checks from the worked example on it and record the source, its date and the date you checked.
